name: Patriot (PAC-3 MSE)
short_role: Long-range, high-altitude air defense battery protecting rear-area cities and infrastructure from ballistic and cruise missile threats.
characteristics: PAC-3 MSE interceptor: hit-to-kill, ~60 km engagement range against ballistic threats, up to ~24-30 km intercept altitude
AN/MPQ-65 phased-array radar: 360° search/track, resistant to jamming, detection well beyond 100 km
Battery: radar set, engagement control station, antenna mast group, 4-8 launcher stations (each holding multiple PAC-3 MSE rounds)
Deployable in under an hour; typically positioned well back from the line to protect high-value rear-area targets
Confirmed intercepts of Russian Kinzhal hypersonic and Iskander ballistic missiles
employment_notes: Positioned in the deep operational/strategic rear, not on the line — its job is theater/point missile defense over cities, power infrastructure, and logistics hubs, cued by a wider integrated air defense network (early warning radar, other SAM layers, passive acoustic/EW sensors) rather than acting alone.
contrast_vs_traditional: In traditional warfare, ground-based air defense mainly countered aircraft. Here the primary threat set is ballistic and hypersonic missiles and mass drone raids, so Patriot batteries are one layer in a networked, multi-tier air defense stack (short-range guns/MANPADS near the line, mid-range SAMs, then Patriot for the highest-end threats) rather than a standalone system — and cost-per-intercept against cheap drones has become a real operational constraint.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: radar cues, launcher fires an interceptor, short intercept vignette against an inbound track.

connections.description: Receives cueing/track data from the wider integrated air defense network.
Resupplied with interceptor missiles and generator fuel from the nearest logistics hub.
